reason: Repository built from scratch per MAYHEM-SPEC-DFAPTI-WATER-001-v2.0. Chose a static JSON data store, a dependency-free Node validation script, and a static HTML/CSS/JS workspace rather than a database or application framework, per spec section 32 (implementation independence) and section 4 (append-only, human-authority principles).
impact: Repository structure fixed as data/ (JSON registers), scripts/ (validation and tooling), site/ (workspace), docs/ (schema and specification). Future work must fit this structure or record a new decision explaining the change.

reason: Case Definition fields jurisdiction and geographic_scope were set at a general level ("New South Wales, Australia" / "Macleay Valley, NSW") rather than naming a specific local government authority, because no evidence has yet been collected to confirm which authority currently holds responsibility for the Willawarrin/Bellbrook supply.
impact: Case Definition fields will not be edited directly once evidence narrows this down, since section 24 identifiers are immutable for the life of the investigation. Any specific authority identified by evidence is recorded as a Chronology or Evidence entry instead.

reason: Git commit identity for this repository was set locally (not globally) to mayhem82 / minkorecovery@gmail.com at the operator's explicit instruction.
impact: Commit authorship in this repository is attributed to mayhem82. No effect on any other repository on this machine.

reason: The Relationship Map (spec section 14) was implemented as a view computed at render time from the cross-reference fields already present on Evidence, Chronology, Contradictions, Open Questions, and Threads, rather than as a new stored register (e.g. data/relationships.json).
impact: There is exactly one place any given relationship is recorded (on the citing record's own link field), preventing the map from drifting out of sync with the registers it summarizes. Documented in docs/DATA_MODEL.md.

reason: The first evidence-collection run (RUN-0001) repeatedly and consistently identified Kempsey Shire Council as the responsible local government authority (EV-0002, EV-0004, EV-0005, EV-0006, EV-0008). Per DEC-0002, the immutable Case Definition fields (jurisdiction, geographic_scope) are not edited to add this now-confirmed detail; it is instead carried by source_authority fields across the Evidence and Source Registers and by the Chronology.
impact: case.json's jurisdiction and geographic_scope fields remain unchanged. current_status was updated from "Active - Evidence Collection Pending" to "Active - Evidence Collection In Progress" and repository_version bumped to 1.1.0, both treated as legitimately mutable tracking fields per docs/DATA_MODEL.md's 'Mutable vs. Append-Only Fields' section, recorded in CHG-0005.

reason: While following up on SRC-0010 (a Kempsey Shire Council page blocked with HTTP 403), a Wayback Machine snapshot was found to exist and a HEAD request to it succeeded, but every GET attempt returned HTTP 498. Rather than continuing to vary request headers, user agents, or other techniques to force the content through, the attempt was stopped and logged as a continued access gap.
impact: Establishes a standing operating rule for this investigation: ordinary, honest HTTP requests (a realistic but truthful User-Agent, standard Accept headers) are fair game, but deliberately working harder to defeat a site's bot-detection is not, even in service of legitimate public-interest research. Blocked sources are recorded as access gaps in the Source Register (see SRC-0010/0011/0012) and flagged for manual, ordinary-browser retrieval rather than further automated workarounds.

reason: A WebSearch result summary asserted the existence of a distinct 'Bellbrook Water Treatment Plant' capital-works project, which would materially resolve Q-0002/THR-14. A second, independent search query's own summary explicitly contradicted this, and the underlying source article could not be fetched to check the primary text (HTTP 403). EV-0013 (RUN-0003), which covers the same $54m water/sewer capital-works program from an actually-fetched and preserved primary source, names new plants at Willawarrin and Crescent Head plus a separate emergency plant at Steuart McIntyre Dam - no Bellbrook-specific plant.
impact: Per spec section 4's Source Before Analysis principle, the 'Bellbrook Water Treatment Plant' claim is not accepted into the Evidence Register on the basis of an unverifiable, self-contradicting search-engine summary that a properly-sourced record (EV-0013) does not corroborate. Q-0002 and THR-14 remain open with no evidence of Bellbrook having received a dedicated treatment plant.

reason: During RUN-0005, this session's fetch tool returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on every URL attempted without exception - including miragenews.com at the exact URL this repository preserved successfully as SRC-0015/EV-0010 in an earlier session, and on completely unrelated control URLs (en.wikipedia.org, example.com) that carry no plausible bot-detection interest in this investigation. This is distinct from DEC-0006's site-specific, deliberate-bot-detection scenario: it is a session-level tooling constraint affecting all outbound fetches, not a property of any particular source.
impact: No source can be preserved or hashed by this session. Leads found via search this run are registered in the Source Register only (preservation_status 'Not Preserved', hash_status 'No Hash') and are not promoted to Evidence Register entries, since this repository's own bar for an evidence item (a real preserved file, ideally hashed) cannot be met right now. A future session with working fetch access should treat SRC-0025/SRC-0026 (and any other 'Not Confirmed - fetch blocked' source added this run) as priority candidates to re-check, rather than assuming they were already tried and failed for a structural reason.

reason: The operator (who holds Human Authority over evidence acceptance per spec section 4) directed that all findings go into the Evidence Register as found, rather than being held at Source Register level only pending a direct fetch/preservation - the practice this repository had followed since DEC-0008 (RUN-0005 onward) because this session's fetch tool has returned HTTP 403 on every URL attempted. This run (RUN-0027) reviewed every source registered since RUN-0005 (SRC-0016 through SRC-0047) and promoted the fourteen that carry a genuine, specific, citable fact (as opposed to sources registered only as "this URL exists but is blocked, no content extracted") to Evidence Register entries EV-0014 through EV-0027.
impact: Going forward, a source with a genuine extracted fact is promoted to Evidence at the time it is found, using verification_state "Requires Verification" (or "Unverified"/"Disputed" as appropriate), classification "Secondary Reference", and a hash_exception_reason documenting that the finding is search-snippet-sourced pending direct preservation - not held back at Source Register level. This is structurally valid per validation rule 10/11 (only "Accepted" evidence requires non-null proof-of-fact). DEC-0008's underlying fetch-tool constraint is unchanged; this decision changes only how this repository responds to it. No question or contradiction is closed/resolved by this run - promoting evidence is distinct from resolving a question, and the existing conservative bar for closing Q-0006/CTR-0001 etc. without a fetched primary source is unchanged.

reason: RUN-0031 initially preserved and promoted six Evidence entries (EV-0031-EV-0036) from a text the operator described as pasted "from their own successful retrieval of the original PDF" (SRC-0042). The operator then clarified the text was actually produced by ChatGPT's text-extraction of the PDF into a DOCX, with ChatGPT's own appended caveat that "complex tables, formatting, and scanned page layouts may not exactly match the original PDF." This is a materially different, lower-confidence provenance than a direct primary-source read, particularly since the caveat specifically flags tables - exactly where this evidence's key figures come from (manganese concentrations, exceedance counts).
impact: EV-0031 through EV-0036 downgraded from classification "Complete"/verification_state "Verified" to "Partial"/"Requires Verification". SRC-0042 downgraded from preservation_status "Preserved" to "Partially Preserved". Establishes a standing rule for this investigation: content obtained via a third-party AI tool's extraction/OCR of a document (as opposed to a direct human read or this session's own fetch of the primary file) is recorded at "Requires Verification"/"Partial" at best, never "Verified"/"Accepted", until independently cross-checked against the original document - regardless of how specific or plausible the extracted figures look. Numeric tables are treated as the highest-risk content type for this kind of provenance.

reason: While checking the operator's report that SRC-0001's live URL now returns HTTP 404, this session audited every Evidence Register entry with a preserved_file_reference by independently computing SHA-256 over the actual file on disk and comparing it to the recorded document_hash. Nine entries from RUN-0001/RUN-0002 (EV-0001, EV-0002, EV-0003, EV-0004, EV-0007, EV-0008, EV-0009, EV-0011, EV-0012) had a document_hash that did NOT match their preserved file. Git history shows each affected file has only ever had a single commit (never modified since first added), so this is not file corruption or drift after the fact - the recorded hash was simply never an accurate SHA-256 of the file when it was first written to the register, for reasons this session cannot determine (most plausibly a hash value that was written without actually running a hashing tool against the real file). Ten other entries from the same original batch (EV-0005, EV-0006, EV-0010, EV-0013) and all of this session's own hashed entries (EV-0031-EV-0036) were independently confirmed correct.
impact: document_hash corrected on all nine affected entries to the actual, independently-verified SHA-256 of their preserved files (the files themselves were not altered - only the hash field, which was simply wrong, was fixed to match reality). classification and verification_state left unchanged since the underlying preserved files appear genuine and unaltered; this was a recording error, not a fabricated or substituted source. Establishes a standing operating rule: any future document_hash entered into this register must be the literal output of a hashing tool (scripts/hash-file.js or equivalent) run against the exact preserved file, never typed or estimated, and this session commits to spot-checking hash integrity periodically going forward given this discovery.

reason: At the operator's suggestion to "use other methods" for evidence collection, this session ran the environment's own proxy diagnostic (curl to the agent-proxy status endpoint, per /root/.ccr/README.md) to check whether the persistent HTTP 403 responses recorded since RUN-0005 (DEC-0008) were a fixable tooling problem. The diagnostic and its documentation confirmed these are 403/407 responses from an organizational egress policy that deliberately does not allow this session to reach the destination hosts (government/council/media domains) - explicitly NOT a certificate, proxy-configuration, or client-bug problem, and the documented guidance is "do not retry or route around it - report the blocked host."
impact: Confirms DEC-0008 was correctly diagnosed as a session-level constraint, now with a specific known cause (deliberate egress policy, not a bug) rather than an unexplained tooling failure. No further attempts will be made to find workarounds around this specific block (e.g., alternate protocols, retries, header variations) - consistent with both this investigation's own DEC-0006 precedent (no deliberate evasion of access controls) and the proxy's explicit operating instructions. This session instead diversified its WebSearch-based methods this run (academic literature via PubMed, first-party company statements, official court records, business registries) rather than re-attempting fetches.

reason: At the operator's directive to try the Internet Archive (Wayback Machine), this session tested two distinct paths: (1) WebFetch directly against a web.archive.org snapshot URL for one of this investigation's key still-unfetched documents, which failed with "Claude Code is unable to fetch from web.archive.org" - a different failure signature from the DEC-0008/DEC-0012 organizational-egress-policy 403s (which return an actual HTTP status from the proxy), consistent with a tool-level restriction rather than a network/session policy block. (2) WebSearch with allowed_domains restricted to web.archive.org, which returned an explicit API error: "The following domains are not accessible to our user agent," linking to Anthropic's own documentation on how site owners block its crawler - confirming this is a platform-level constraint (archive.org/Wayback Machine blocks Anthropic's crawler/fetcher), not a fixable session configuration issue, and not the same underlying cause as DEC-0008/DEC-0012.
impact: Internet Archive / Wayback Machine is confirmed NOT accessible from this session via either WebFetch or WebSearch, for a documented, distinct, non-fixable reason. This closes off Wayback Machine as a workaround path for any of this investigation's many fetch-blocked primary sources (consistent with DEC-0006's original finding from RUN-0002, now re-confirmed with a clearer technical explanation rather than an unexplained HTTP 498). No further attempts should be made to fetch web.archive.org or search it via allowed_domains in future runs; this session returned to general WebSearch-based methods for the remainder of this run.

reason: The operator corrected this session's recent run cadence: several prior runs (e.g. RUN-0058, RUN-0060) tried only 3-4 searches on a single narrow sub-topic before concluding "No relevant change detected" and closing the run. The operator noted this is inconsistent with the investigation's own name and methodology - Deep Forensic All Paths Taken Investigation - which calls for each pass to work through the full set of currently open questions and active threads, not sample one angle and stop.
impact: Standing rule going forward: each DFAPTI run should sweep every open question (Q-, CTR-) and every active (non-Not-Started, non-Closed) thread for at least one genuinely fresh search angle before the run is considered complete, rather than exhausting a single sub-topic and stopping there. A run may still legitimately end with mostly "no relevant change" outcomes - that is honest and expected once a question is search-exhausted - but the breadth of what was tried should span the case's full open surface each time, not one thread in isolation. RUN-0061 was the first run under this corrected practice, sweeping 20 search angles across 5 open questions and 5 threads in a single pass.

reason: The operator shared a set of repository-improvement suggestions attributed to another AI system (Gemini), including three complete GitHub Actions workflow files: a scheduled scraper/ingestion job, a "case_files/*.md" YAML-frontmatter/hash linter, and a static SUMMARY.md dashboard generator. On inspection, all three assumed a repository structure this investigation does not have (a case_files/ directory of Markdown files with YAML frontmatter, a src/ingest_records.py scraper) rather than this repo's actual structure (flat JSON registers in data/, validated by scripts/validate.js, browsable via the deployed GitHub Pages workspace). The frontmatter/audit workflow and the dashboard workflow would have silently no-op'd (globbing zero files) rather than actually checking or summarizing anything; the ingestion workflow additionally referenced a nonexistent GitHub Action (actions/python-versions@v5) and called a script that does not exist in this repository.
impact: Declined implementing the three suggested workflows as given. Implemented one real equivalent instead: .github/workflows/validate.yml, which runs the existing node scripts/validate.js (this repo's actual 17-rule structural validator) on every push/PR to main. Standing guidance: externally-suggested tooling/workflow changes should be checked against this repository's actual file structure and existing scripts before adoption, not implemented on the assumption that generic "evidence repository" best-practice templates apply directly - a workflow that silently no-ops or fails outright is worse than no workflow, since it looks like coverage without providing any.

reason: The operator requested three infrastructure enhancements: (1) formalize a general, case-agnostic MAYHEM specification usable by other investigations, since until now the only specification document was case-specific (docs/specs/MAYHEM-SPEC-DFAPTI-WATER-001-v2.0.md); (2) automate the Relationship Map (spec section 14/31), which the workspace has always computed dynamically from cross-reference fields in app.js but never exposed as a static, regenerable artifact; (3) turn the repository into a GitHub Template repository so other investigators could use it to start new cases.
impact: Implemented (1) and (2) in this run. Wrote SPEC.md at the repository root: a generalized, case-agnostic MAYHEM specification derived from the existing case-specific document, with an added Appendix A documenting failure modes this specification exists to prevent (manufactured evidence, AI-summary conflation, provenance drift, untrustworthy hashes, silent workaround of access controls, scope creep) - drawn directly from failure modes this investigation actually encountered and caught (see DEC-0008, DEC-0010, DEC-0011, DEC-0013, DEC-0014, DEC-0015, and the RUN-0028/RUN-0042/RUN-0061 stale-content rejections). Cross-linked README.md and the case-specific spec to point to SPEC.md. Wrote scripts/generate-relationship-map.js, mirroring app.js's buildRelationshipEdges/buildNodeLabels logic exactly, which generates docs/RELATIONSHIP_MAP.md: one Mermaid flowchart per Investigation Thread (a single full-graph diagram was rejected as unreadable at this register's size - 292 raw edge references across 71 evidence, 32 chronology, and 15 thread records) plus one thread-dependency graph. Added .github/workflows/relationship-map.yml to regenerate and auto-commit this file on any push to main that touches data/ or the generator script itself, mirroring the style of the existing deploy-pages.yml and validate.yml workflows. Item (3), the GitHub Template Repository setting, was NOT implemented in this run - it is a public-facing repository-branding change (not a content change) for a live investigation that touches an active coronial death inquiry and Aboriginal community history, and is being explicitly raised with the operator for confirmation before being flipped, rather than actioned silently.

reason: The operator clarified the intended gating model: DFAPTI (the evidence register) is live and keeps moving; DFAPTA and every stage downstream of it only advance on an explicit freeze command, producing a new numbered cycle each time rather than silently tracking the live register. The operator also clarified that analysis is not a dead end - DFAPTA surfaces new open questions that feed back into DFAPTI's own open_questions.json, closing the loop between analysis and further evidence collection. Acting on the second half of that: reviewed DFAPTA Cycle 1's disclosure requests and path boundaries for gaps not already covered by Q-0001 through Q-0006, and added three that are genuinely new and evidence-groundable: Q-0007 (why the villages remain on standalone extraction rather than main-network connection/redundancy, from AR-018), Q-0008 (the missing 2021-2022/2022-2023 annual reports and unstable report-series naming, from EV-0065), and Q-0009 (LC Water's contractual commissioning deadline and acceptance criteria for Willawarrin, from AR-012 - directly relevant to assessing Q-0001 against an actual contractual benchmark rather than only the publicly announced target). Declined to convert DFAPTA's more normative/aspirational disclosure requests (e.g. a 'lived-experience register', a 'cross-community equity assessment') into open questions - those are advocacy asks, not investigable factual questions with a locatable evidentiary answer, and belong in Enforcement Notice/Advocacy Package rather than the evidence register's open-question mechanism.
impact: open_questions.json grows from 6 to 9 entries. No evidence added by this decision itself. Establishes a repeatable pattern: each future DFAPTA cycle should be checked for genuinely new, evidence-answerable questions before being considered complete, not just read passively.

reason: While building a new Actions to Take view (a derived checklist inside DFAPTI, distinct from Enforcement Notice), testing surfaced a mistake in RUN-0065: SRC-0106 was created for the 2019-2020 Drinking Water Management System Annual Report URL, but that exact URL was already registered as SRC-0047 since 2026-07-29 - RUN-0065 didn't check the existing source register before adding it, producing a duplicate. Corrected: removed SRC-0106, merged its update into SRC-0047 (last_checked and a note recording that EV-0072 is now its first evidence entry), and softened EV-0072's description, which had overstated the URL as newly 'located via search' rather than accurately describing it as an already-registered source that had no evidence entry yet. RUN-0065's own automation_log entry is left as originally written, per this repository's append-only discipline - it still references SRC-0106 by name, which is now a correction trail rather than a live source.
impact: source_register.json returns to 106 entries (SRC-0106 removed). No evidence was removed - EV-0072 and CHR-0033 from RUN-0065 remain valid and unaffected. Establishes a concrete lesson for future runs: check source_register.json for an existing URL before registering a new source_id for it.

reason: A second case (DFAPTI-MNC-2026-00001, Mid North Coast PolAir-Remote drone expansion) was added to this repository, resolving the open question this README had deliberately left unanswered since the repository's earliest structure: whether a second case's evidence data lives under cases/<CASE-ID>/data/ or gets its own repository. Chose the former - a per-case data/ directory - to keep the "mayhem investigations only, no other repo" operating constraint intact and to keep the cases/<CASE-ID>/ site-structure pattern already built for the six-stage workspace consistent for every future case. This case (DFAPTI-BB-2026-00001) deliberately keeps its existing data/ location at the repository root rather than being moved into cases/DFAPTI-BB-2026-00001/data/, to avoid rewriting the several hundred already-committed cross-references, preserved/ filenames, and the live GitHub Pages deployment's existing fetch paths for no functional benefit - it becomes the one grandfathered exception, not the new pattern. scripts/case-registry.js now lists every case's data directory explicitly; scripts/validate.js and scripts/generate-relationship-map.js run independently per case; scripts/resume.js, add-source.js, and log-run.js take an optional --case flag (defaulting to this case, to keep every existing operator habit and doc example working unchanged).
impact: No files in this case's own data/, preserved/, or workspace pages changed location or content. scripts/validate.js and scripts/generate-relationship-map.js now iterate every registered case; docs/RELATIONSHIP_MAP.md gained a per-case section structure. README.md's repository-layout section and its 'Adding a case' note were rewritten to state the resolved architecture instead of posing it as an open question.
